newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money eases to 3.00/3.10 percent.
newsitem.headline: German call money eases to 3.00/3.10 percent.

text.p: German call money rates fell to 3.00/3.10 percent on Thursday from 3.10/3.125 on Wednesday as cash levels rose.
Dealers said most trades were done at 3.08 percent. "There's a surplus of cash," one dealer said. He predicted call money rates would stay unchanged ahead of the weekend.
The rise in liquidity levels was reflected in an increase in commercial bank reserves at the Bundesbank which stood at 42.3 billion marks on Wednesday, up from Tuesday's 39 billion.
The average for the month through Wednesday was 40.2 billion marks, up from 40.0 billion marks.
Borrowings from the Bundesbank's Lombard facility on Wednesday totalled about 600 million marks after being negligible the day before.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA= was 3.11900 percent on Thursday, down from 3.13200 percent on Wednesday.
